newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. Treasuries mixed in directionless Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries mixed in directionless Tokyo.

text.p: Cash U.S. Treasuries firmed slightly, while futures eased by Tokyo midday on Friday, following a sharp recovery overnight, traders said.

"T-bond futures were easier on light profit-taking, but the market is lacking direction this morning," a Japanese bank trader said. "The PPI results (due for release at 1230 GMT) should determine the near-term trends."

Traders said the market was sluggish, but market sentiment brightened after Treasury prices jumped in New York overnight as U.S. retail sales fell for three consecutive months for the first time in 15 years.
"It seems that the credit-tightening speculation in July is fading further after looking at the results of recent economic indicators," the trader said.
Another trader said that more short holders are expected to cover their positions actively if the results of the PPI data turn out to be lower than forecast.
The key 6-5/8 percent 30-year bond stood at 98-4/32, yielding 6.77 percent, compared with 98-2/32 in New York.
The September T-bond futures contract fell 1/32 from the previous close to 111-11/32 by late morning. It moved in a range of 111-8/32 to 111-12/32.
